newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Aston Villa join UK soccer club share league.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Aston Villa join UK soccer club share league.

text.p: Former European champions Aston Villa, joining Britain's growing league of soccer club shares, on Thursday announced details of a 125 million pound ($200 million) stock market flotation.
Villa, based in the English Midlands city of Birmingham, are asking fans and professional investors to pay 11 pounds per share for a stake of almost 16 percent in the Premier League club.

The issue should raise more than 15 million pounds to finance improvements to the Villa Park stadium and recruit new players. Club chairman Doug Ellis stands to make almost four million pounds as he cuts his stake in the club from around 47 percent to just over a third.

Villa will be the fourth largest British soccer stock after English champions Manchester United, which has a market value of more than 400 million pounds, and Chelsea and Newcastle United, worth around 180 million pounds each.
It will be the 16th British club to float.

Shares in the sector rocketed in value last year but have fallen in recent weeks as euphoria surrounding the potential revenue from pay-per-view television rights is replaced by a more selective approach.
Shares in Newcastle, floated earlier this month, are now trading at a discount to their 135 pence issue price.
Villa finance director Mark Ansell said he believed that demand from leading investment institutions was likely to outstrip supply.
"Institutions have distinguished Aston Villa from a number of other clubs in the sector," he said. "It is seen as a quality investment which is being run as a good business."

Share analyst Nick Batram of brokers Greig Middleton said the stock looked fairly expensive compared with others in the sector but agreed that the club appeared a sound business. "It is one of the bigger clubs, well-managed, with a good stadium and large catchment area for fans," he said.
Villa, fifth in the Premier League and on course for a place in next season's UEFA Cup, forecast a pre-tax profit of 2.78 million pounds in the year to end-May, on turnover of 21.16 million.
A quarter of the shares being issued have been set aside for ordinary fans, who must invest a minimum of 440 pounds. Season ticket holders and club employees will be given priority.

The club plans to spend five million pounds this year on a 650-seat conference and banqueting suite at its stadium and to install two giant video screens pitch-side at the Euro '96 venue. The balance of 10 million pounds will be available for squad strengthening.
